title: Small phrases, said right
goal: Use everyday phrases the way native speakers say them
intro: Much of fluent English is fixed phrases: “on the way”, “in time”, “at the end”, “take a photo”, “by mistake”. Getting one small word wrong (“in the way”, “give an exam”) is enough to sound unnatural. Here are the everyday ones Indian speakers most often mix up.

rules.rule: take an exam (write it); pass / fail an exam; take a photo, take a break.
examples: I’m taking my driving test on Monday.

rules.rule: on time = punctual; in time = early enough.
examples: We got there in time to see the start.

rules.rule: by mistake, by chance, on purpose, on the way, in a hurry.
examples: I’ll pick up milk on the way.

rules.rule: at the end (of something) vs in the end (finally).
examples: at the end of the film
In the end, we stayed home.

mistakes.why: In international English you take an exam; examiners give it.

mistakes.wrong: I am on the way to reach.

ex.q: Can you ___ a picture of me here?
I sent the email to the wrong person ___.

ex.y: on time = at the planned time

ex.q: I’m ___. I’ll be there in ten minutes.
She is ___ her final exams next month.
I will give the exam next week.
ex.fixed: I will take the exam next week.

ex.q: He broke the glass in purpose.
ex.fixed: He broke the glass on purpose.

ex.q: At the end, we decided to stay home.
ex.fixed: In the end, we decided to stay home.

ex.q: We reached the cinema just ___ time for the film.

ex.a: Let's take a short break and get some tea.

a: Please take a photo of us
Could you take a photo of us
ex.y: Please take a photo of us.

talk: Describe your last exam or interview day from start to end: whether you were on time, what happened on the way, and how it went in the end.
